sentences.text: Shri Himanshu Tiwari - learned counsel for the appel  Shri Ajay Shukla - learned Government Advocate for t State.
Heard on I.A. No. 18245 of 2025 , which is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 368 days in the filing the instant appeal.
In view of the grounds mentioned therein, aforesaid I.A. is allowed.
Delay is condoned.
The appeal is admitted for final hearing.
Learned Government Advocate adopts objections filed for co-accused Rajkumar Panika.
Heard on I.A. No. 8373 of 2025 , which is first application under Section 430(1) of B.N.S.S., 20213 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

This appeal is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 31.01.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012), Shahdol (M.P.) in S.T. No. 284 of 2021 whereby the appellant has 2 CRA-3584-2025 been convicted under Section 5(G) r/w 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and sentenced to R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-; in lieu 1 year additional R.I.
Though the appellant has also been convicted under Section 376(D) of IPC but has not been separately sentenced.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
There are general and omnibus allegations against the present appellant.

The main accused in this case is Rajkumar Baiga, who has already been granted bail by this Court Aitu Biga vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68664862/
1 vide order dated 07.02.2025.

sentences.text: There are good chances of success of the appeal.

It is, therefore,
prayed that sentence of the appellant be suspended and he be granted bail.
Learned Government Advocate, on the other hand, opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, without commenting on the merits of the case, we are of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No. 8373 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that on depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the Trial Court on 09.12.2025 and such other dates as may be fixed by the Trial Court, the execution of remaining part of jail sentence imposed upon the appellant Aitu 3 CRA-3584-2025 Baiga shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till final disposal of the appeal.
C. C. as per rules.
 (VIVEK AGARWAL)
